goal: Implement system-level evaluation block in federated.py with global store aggregation and system-level attack records
summary: Phase 1 complete. Added a full system-level evaluation block to src/fed_rag/evaluators/federated.py after the existing client-level blocks. The block builds global knowledge stores from combined client data and runs all 4 DRAG-compatible attacks (data poisoning, membership inference, knowledge extraction, node availability) at the system level, producing 4 new matrix records prefixed with 'System ...'. Also fixed a pre-existing bug where node availability evaluations passed the original dataset (lacking client_id) to evaluate_rag_answers, causing dropped_clients/byzantine_clients filtering to have no effect — both client and system node availability blocks now correctly use _flatten(clients). End-to-end evaluator run produced 8 records (4 client + 4 system) with correct degradation metrics. All existing security tests pass.
stepSummaries:
1. Add system-level evaluation block after the client-level node-availability block in federated.py, reusing _build_store, _flatten, and existing attack classes [verified]
  2. Run federated evaluator with all four attacks enabled and confirm >4 records in output JSON [verified]
  3. Run existing security tests to ensure no regressions [verified]
